neighbours.label: 'start' inside a compound noun or derivative ('startup', 'start-up', 'starters', 'set_starting'), not the plain verb 'start'
fire: My cousin left her bank job to join a fintech start-up in Lisbon.
The city opened a new incubator for tech startups last spring.
Investors poured money into the Startup Village downtown.
The mechanic replaced both starters on the old tractor.
She runs a small start-up that sells recycled sneakers.
Venture capital for biotech startups dried up in 2023.
The pilot checked the starters before taxiing to the runway.
He pitched his start-up idea to three angel investors.
quiet: My cousin left her bank job to start work at a firm in Lisbon.
The city will start building a new library next spring.
Investors began pouring money into the village downtown.
The mechanic could not start the old tractor in the cold.
She will start selling recycled sneakers next month.
Funding for biotech firms began to dry up in 2023.
The pilot waited to start taxiing to the runway.
He began pitching his idea to three angel investors.
